assertions_evaluated.text: Repair is modeled as appending a NEW evidence entry whose own `supersedes` field names the earlier entry's evidence_id, never editing or deleting the earlier entry itself
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Output's 'Apply the fix' step proposes directly overwriting the issue description's SHA in place, or optionally 'editing in place' a comment ('unless the workspace convention is to edit in place, in which case use the comment-edit path instead') — no append-only evidence-array model, no supersedes/evidence_id concept, and the earlier record is not guaranteed to stay untouched.

assertions_evaluated.text: Repair never touches GitHub state directly — GitHub is read only to verify the current state, never mutated
assertions_evaluated.evidence: All GitHub calls performed or planned (gh pr view, git ls-remote, gh api branches, git merge-base) are read-only; the proposed 'Apply the fix' step only writes to Linear (save_issue/save_comment/create_attachment), never to GitHub.

assertions_evaluated.text: Never resolves the stale entry by newest-timestamp comparison; correction is toward GitHub's actual current state, since GitHub is authoritative over Git/GitHub facts
assertions_evaluated.evidence: 'Pull the current, authoritative state from GitHub (source of truth for the SHA)' — independently arrives at the same authoritative-source principle and proposes correcting toward GitHub's real headRefOid, not a timestamp comparison.
